What it does: A checkbox. When it's on, copies stand at right angles to the ground, leaning with a hillside, as grass and rocks often do. Trees usually look better upright, with it off.
How far every copy leans, in degrees from upright. Each copy leans in its own direction.
How much more each copy may lean, at random, in degrees. 10 to 15 keeps grass from standing too straight.
A checkbox. When it's on, each copy is turned a random amount around the up direction, so they don't all face the same way.
A turn, in degrees, that every copy gets around the up direction, added to its random turn. With random turn off, it turns every copy to face the same way, such as a row of fences.
For a card: how many pictures stand at each copy, from 1 to 3, each turned its own way. 1 suits grass painted densely; 2 or 3 make loose bunches.
